I've had many fruit/nut mixes in my 58 years. Most were delightful. So when I saw the variety & quantity/price of this item, & immediately purchased it. Upon opening the bag I felt then looked to see separate clumps of raisins, all the same size, which told me they were hand-measured, weighed then moved on to the next step. So the raisins in this mix are about 4-5 golf balls that are so squeezed together, soft & moist that separating them was a sticky mess, resulting in smaller clumps, but no total separation. They simply stuck together to the point of becoming clumps of raisins resulting in one big raising for each inseparable clump.
Nest, I took a small amount of as much of everything in the bag that I could combine. To my disappointment, everything tasted the same except the peanuts, which are the predominant flavor of this combination. The resulting flavor can be described in 1 word-BITTER. I was astounded that all of these wonderful fruits & nuts literally lacked flavor in its entirety. Bitter & no flavor. Shocking, when you consider the variety, which is one of if not THE widest variety of fruits in 1 mix I've ever come across in a processed product of this type. I like to use these mixes mainly on cereals, but this 1 is going back. Seems like the quality is subpar, resulting in a very disappointing bitter bag of bung.

An NIH-funded research team led by Dr. Stanley Hazen at the Cleveland Clinic examined the relationship between erythritol and heart attacks and stroke. In an initial study with more than 1,000 people, the team looked for compounds in blood whose levels were linked to future cardiac risk. They tracked major adverse cardiovascular events over three years, including death and nonfatal heart attack or stroke. Results appeared in Nature Medicine on February 27, 2023.

The team found that elevated levels of erythritol and several related artificial sweeteners were associated with the risk for cardiovascular events. To confirm this result, the researchers examined two more groups of people in the U.S. and Europe totaling almost 3,000. They also developed a method to better distinguish erythritol from related compounds.

These measurements reproduced the association between erythritol and cardiovascular events. People with the highest erythritol levels (top 25%) were about twice as likely to have cardiovascular events over three years of follow-up.

I waited until after I'd eaten some of this cheese a half dozen times at least, before doing this review, so as to give it every benefit of the doubt, and also in hopes that I might change my mind and maybe the taste would improve. However, no matter how many different times I ate some, nor what I ate it with, did it change my opinion, this was just plain and simple, a huge disappointment, to say the least, and not only in taste, but also in texture, which was equally as bad. Since you're obviously not able to taste it first, I've never had very good luck with buying cheese on-line, so I was very hesitant about buying this cheese, but my decision to do so was based entirely on so many good reviews. I always read the reviews on most products I buy on-line, and especially if it's some item I've never had before, which usually pays off to do so, but this was definitely an exception. I have absolutely no offer of an explanation as to why so many reviews are in stark contrast to my own, other than the possibility that maybe the majority of people giving such good reviews have just never tasted really good Colby cheese. I like to consider myself, on a small scale, somewhat of a Cheese Connoisseur for a couple of reasons; one simply because I do love & eat a lot of cheese, but also (in this case) because Colby is my favorite type cheese. In my opinion, this particular Colby cheese not only had very little taste, but also had a very rubbery texture to it. However, I believe it's important to note that this cheese did not have a bad taste, but it simply didn't have a good taste either. Which I guess, the fact that it didn't have a bad taste, would warrant the single star review/rating (as opposed to zero stars), but also made it possible to still eat it, without having to throw it out and making it a total loss. I have had cheese that tasted bad enough that I couldn't eat it at all, making it a total waste of money, which wasn't the case here. This place does an excellent job at packaging & shipping, and this cheese shipped with cold packs, which were still very cold when I received it. Plus, the cheese looked very fresh and had good color to it, all the things you want to see when you buy cheese, but unfortunately, in this case none of those things made a difference! The taste was just very bland and lacked that good creamy taste that a real good Colby can sometimes have, unfortunately. And granted, a Colby cheese tends to always be a bit rubbery, especially more so, than like a Cheddar is, but in this case the texture was very rubbery, making it an even bigger disappointment than the bland taste was. Given all the great reviews, on top of the fact that this cheese came from Wisconsin (which is known to be the Cheese Capital), I really had high hopes going into this purchase (not cheap, by the way), but in my opinion, it was very clearly, a swing & a miss! Something else that might be noteworthy, is that about 5 years ago while on a vacation trip, I discovered a small place that processes & sells many types of cheese, and I found a wonderful Colby there that literally puts this Colby to shame, but unfortunately, it's about 125 miles round trip to go there from where I live, and you can only buy so much cheese at one time. I did notice that several of the reviews mentioned that this Colby makes great grilled cheese sandwiches, and I'm sure that's probably possible, but as far as eating it straight up, I would never recommend this Colby to anyone, especially given the high price point!

This particular jar of mayonnaise may be rancid (its expiration date is July 3, 2015); in any case, it left a hideous, oily aftertaste that lasted for hours. Please do not eat these without speaking to your doctor first! Take notice the images and the text do not display the Potassium anywhere. Each wrap contains 15,510mg of Potassium (330%) and an adult is only to consume 3,500mg-4,500mg/day (different countries have different recommendations). Unless your Potassium is dangerously low already, do not put your life in danger. Per Healthline.com: "Symptoms of high potassium depend on the level of the mineral in your blood. You may not have any symptoms at all. But if your potassium levels are high enough to cause symptoms, you may have:
- tiredness or weakness
- a feeling of numbness or tingling
- nausea or vomiting
- trouble breathing
- chest pain
- palpitations or irregular heartbeats

In extreme cases, high potassium can cause paralysis or heart failure. If left untreated, high potassium levels can cause your heart to stop."

Per the words of the seller, "Statements regarding dietary supplements have not been evaluated by the FDA and are not intended to diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any disease or health condition"

Note: If you purchase these and need to return them, the Amazon website will state it is not returnable, but that is not true. Contact Amazon Support and they will refund your money. There is no need to contact the seller.

Disclaimer to this review: I ordered this, received it perfectly, but never tasted it. So, my review is not so much a review, but feedback intended to help others like me, who learned after the fact that I should have done more research before making the purchase. As stated, the product arrived perfectly packaged, and I can't say enough good things about the company's customer service.  This feedback is for those who, like me, knew very little about Kim Chi, thought they would like it and had no idea about the extreme pungency of the food. I erroneously assumed that because I like other pickled vegetables that I would like this. But Kim Chi shouldn't be compared to things like sauerkraut. One look at the package, combined with the foul odor (yes, odor), and I realized that I would not be able to get past it. That odor lingers too ....on and around everything it comes in contact with. And now that I have done a bit more homework on it, I have also learned that it lingers on your breath as well. I think if you like it - and clearly thousands of people do - then that's great. If you have a strong sensitivity to the smell of food, and you have not tried Kim Chi, just be very aware of what you're getting into. Footnote: In conversing with the company and learning about this 'normal,' odor, I never asked for a refund. On the contrary, I felt it was my own fault for not doing more research. Still, they did refund my purchase and shipping costs. I find that level of customer service very admirable.  My vote of one star is for my personal experience with the product. If I could rate the company, I would give them five stars indeed.

Let me preface by saying I LOVE the normal Spry Cinnamon mints. So I assumed the Cinnamon Power mints would be even better. I was wrong. The power mints somehow manage to burn my mouth and tongue (have to keep moving mint around) while providing minimal flavor. I'm not sure if I got a bad batch or that is how they are supposed to be. Above the UPC is PMC70 R3 - maybe that is the batch number.

So I did a little experimenting and kept adding sugar into my mouth while the mint was in - this enabled me to taste the flavor. I then crushed a mint with 1/2 tsp of sugar and ate that. I bought this hoping it would be my new extreme hot sauce. Over the years I have collected scores or hot sauces, and make sure I have one that I test as "the hottest." Because I have been testing sauces for years, I have plateaued - I cannot seem to find anything hotter than my current "hottest" sauce (Da Bomb). Prior to Da Bomb, my hottest sauce was Demon Ichor, and prior to that was Mad Dog 357 (the one with the bullet key ring). Da Bomb is barely hotter than Demon Ichor, and Demon Ichor burns for twice as long.

Blair's 3am is nowhere near as hot as Da Bomb. Not even close. On top of that, it is really intended as a collectible item that is never opened. Getting past the wax is a chore - search Google/YouTube and you will see it mentioned many times. Once the wax is off, a cork is used to stop the bottle. Unfortunately, due to capillary action or some other magic, hot sauce seeps from inside the bottle (there is a thin film from when you pour out a drop), past the cork, which then covers the cork with the sauce. You cannot open the bottle without getting sauce all over your hand.

Don't get me wrong, the sauce is hot. Like all the extreme sauces, it is really a cooked-down extract with an oily consistency. Flavor is mild, habanero-type flavor, and it is quite hot. But it nowhere near as hot as Da Bomb, or Demon Ichor, or Mad Dog. It is a liability once opened due to the use of a cork.

I got one of the sample packs sold on the Teeccino website that includes Java, Hazelnut, Mocha, Vanilla Nut, Orange, Almond Amaretto, Chocolate Mint, Chai, French Roast and Chocolate in trial size packs that brew (less than) three cups of herbal coffee. I don't know if it was how I brewed it in the drip coffee maker I have, or it's just not enough product in the bag but you won't get what they advertise (6 cups in a drip coffee maker or 30 fluid oz.). I am a huge fan of espresso and black coffee but a friend suggested this and so I caved in. In my opinion, the flavors I have tried (chocolate, java, and chai) taste like incredibly watered down coffee. The chai flavor had an overwhelmingly weird taste (I'm not a fan of chai tea anyway) and the chocolate didn't taste like chocolate at all. After a few days of drinking this pretty regularly, I started getting bad stomach pains, frequent runs to the bathroom, and moderate nausea. It wasn't until I started backtracking that I found it was the Teeccino causing my issues because it has a lot of chicory root, meaning it has a lot of soluble fiber. I have a sensitive digestive system, gastroparesis, and no gall bladder so I have to keep my fiber intake low and here I was drinking loads of it and getting extremely dehydrated. Also in my research, I noted that it has barley listed high on the ingredient list of pretty much every flavor which is a gluten. This product is NOT for those on a gluten or fiber restricted diet or a low residue diet.

Like the reviewer Erin Throm from December 4, 2012, I too purchased this coffee because it is stated in the product description that it is "Swiss Water Decaffeinated," which is what I want, as opposed to the chemical method of decaffeination. I mean, seriously, what's the point of buying organic coffee (coffee is one of the most heavily sprayed crops), if the manufacturer is just going to defile it by using chemicals to decaffeinate it?

Upon receiving my coffee, and noting that the decaffeination method is not displayed anywhere on the bag, I called Seattle's Best and asked what the decaffeination method is. The CSR conferred with his supervisor, and came back and said they couldn't find the information. Red flag #1.

Undaunted, I went to the website, got the customer service email address, and sent the following message on July 25, 2013: "Can you please tell me by what method is the "Decaf Organic Fair Trade Medium-Dark & Rich Level 4" coffee is decaffeinated? I called your 800 customer service number and the representative did not have that information available to him, and even double-checked with his supervisor. Even if it takes a while to research and find out definitively, I don't mind waiting for an answer."

Less than an hour later, this is the reply I received from Mark M.: "I appreciate you taking the time to share your thoughts with us. Unfortunately, the information you are requesting is proprietary information, which we are unable to divulge. I apologize for any inconvenience this may cause. Thanks again for writing us. If you ever have any questions or concerns in the future, please don't hesitate to get in touch." Red flag #2.

Of course that was an unacceptable answer, so I responded as such: "Thanks, Mark. The reason I asked is that due to an autoimmune disease, I am attempting to eliminate as many chemicals from my diet as possible. While I respect "proprietary," can you at least reassure me that the decaffeination process for your organic coffee is chemical free? I would like to support Seattle's Best with my consumer dollars, so I don't think I am asking too much in return with regards to the reassurance I am requesting. Thanks in advance for your reply."

And... this is the reply I received: "You can find all nutritional value of out beverages at this link, [link removed, Amazon won't allow links from what I understand]. Thanks again for writing us. If you ever have any questions or concerns in the future, please don't hesitate to get in touch." And... of course I clicked the link and the method of decaffeination was conspicuously absent. Red flag #3.

All in all I give this coffee four stars because the taste is very good. However, I deduct three stars for their covert way in which the company refuses to divulge the decaffeination method. Now, if you were a manufacturer of decaffeinated organic coffee, wouldn't you be proud to state that your organic decaf was naturally decaffeinated and not chemically decaffeinated? Therefore, left to my own conclusions, I have to conclude that this coffee is not proudly naturally decaffeinated, but shamefully chemically decaffeinated, and that's why the big secret of not telling us how it's decaffeinated.

After further research, I have discovered that Green Mountain Coffee has a couple of varieties of organic decaf, and they are not shy in advertising that their coffee is water process decaffeinated. That's the one I'll be buying from now on.

Not edible. Do not eat this... craft dust.

First clue: "For decorative use only."
Second clue: No ingredients list as required for all edibles by the FDA.
Third clue: It does not say EDIBLE on the label. (And note, this seller, "Luster Dusts" does not photograph the complete label on their product page.)

Here is an excerpt from the FDA's guidelines:

"Bakers should carefully check the label of decorative products they consider for use on foods. Companies that make edible glitters and dusts are required by law to include a list of ingredients on the label. Common ingredients in edible glitter or dust include sugar, acacia (gum arabic), maltodextrin, cornstarch, and color additives specifically approved for food use, including mica-based pearlescent pigments and FD&C colors such as FD&C Blue No. 1. Most edible glitters and dusts also state “edible” on the label. Is there any actual yeast in this? I have used this many times from several different batches. Each time I was careful to make sure that it was nowhere near the expiration date. Update May 2012:

I have been experimenting with this brand of yeast by trying to activate in the following manner. Take one packet (about two teaspoons), add 1/4 teaspoon of sugar and 1/4 cup of water between 110 and 120 degrees. Put it in a coffee cup and get it all nice and wet and wait about five minutes. Red Star brand and Fleischmans (regular and fast rising) and the Hodgson Mill yeast in their bread machine mixes (the only other ones I have checked) yeast will rise and fill half the coffee mug. (Fast risers fill the whole cup) This brands increases its volume by just a little.

I have also found that Red Star (regular, did not try the fast rise) yeast that is more than one year past its expiration date performs nearly as well as the fresh stuff. Therefore I can say with the confidence of empirical evidence that Red Star yeast that is more than one year past the expiration on the package performs better (read: acceptable) than the packets of unexpired SAF yeast I have tried (read: unacceptable).

Cucina & Amore Pistachio Biscotti is exactly the same made-for-America "Italian" product as ASIN B01N0Z9T66 - Sclafani Pistachio Biscotti. They both must be manufactured by the same counterfeit folks involved in the fake olive oil racket in Italy. I ordered both brands (same exact product) in my desperate search for a replacement bag of the delicious, authentic biscotti I had found for $1.99 in a markdown store: Dolciaria Gadeschi Cantuccini Biscotti. Evidently I'll probably have to go to Europe to get more of this authentic biscotti, which is light and airy but crisp, loaded with 19% nuts (and no filler), and not overly sweet. Until then, the non-traditional Trader Joe's Soft Bite Mini Almond Biscotti will have to do.

Both the Cucina & Amore and the Sclafani brands are yellow in color, hard as a rock, overly sweet, and loaded with candied citrus pieces that get stuck in your teeth. I wish I had been able to see the ingredients before ordering. When dipped in coffee, the biscotti turn to sog in a millisecond. The candied citrus pieces become even more gooey after being dipped. Why candied citrus in biscotti anyway? The candied citrus follows pistachio in the ingredients list, but it overwhelms the texture and taste. Without the candied citrus, both these biscotti brands would still be horrible.

Ingredients: Wheat flour, sugar, eggs, pistachio (8-10%), candied citrus (citrus peels, glucose-fructose syrup, sucrose, acidity regulator/lemon juice concentrate/citric acid, flavors), baking powder (sodium diphosphate, sodium hydrogen carbonate), butter milk, honey, natural flavors, salt.

This company has tricky packaging. They have “100% GRASS-FED VENISON” printed in all caps, causing you to think that’s what you're getting, with “made with” in microscopic type just above it qualifying that statement. If you’re trying to buy a pure product, and/or if you're trying to avoid beef, in all likelihood you’ll be duped. To add further confusion, the company also manufactures pure venison products with identical packaging. Sketchy. Many people do not eat beef for religious reasons and some people have food sensitivities to beef, so I find this totally irresponsible.

To make matters worse, the beef included has no qualifiers: it does not state that it is grass-fed also, it’s just beef, from who knows where. This is the second ingredient, so it makes you wonder what you’re really eating. Not good.

I’ll also add that wild deer do not eat a grass-fed diet, grass is nutritionally incomplete for them, as they also need a wide variety of green plants as well as acorns and nuts for protein, so grass-fed deer meat seems dubious.

While these may very be well made teas, I have to express my disappointment. I am an avid tea drinker and brew a variety of loose leaf teas--herbal and otherwise--throughout the week, and I found all four of these very distasteful to my palate to the point that I am unwilling to use more than the two teaspoons worth I used to brew a small pot of each tea. I honestly wish they weren't all opened so I could return them. The Lavender based one was the least distasteful, but all of them left a sour aftertaste on my tongue. Looking at the ingredients, I think perhaps it was too much of the lemon peel? The sour taste was most certainly very strong (as lemon generally is), and it was an ingredient all four had in common. It seems strange that ALL four teas had the same sourness to them. Either it was a like ingredient or another factor, as they were all brewed per the instructions: water brought to temperature in a kettle, poured into a porcelain teapot, allowed to steep for just over ten minutes, and drunk from a china cup. Many reviewers seem to love them, though, so I guess it's a taste that others enjoy. As I said, I cannot vouch for the quality of the teas in the sense of how they are made, but only to my taste buds, and I found them all to be something I am unwilling to drink. I would personally go elsewhere to be on the safe side.

EDIT: Though it was originally shown as "not eligible for return," I showed Amazon the satisfaction guarantee listed in the item's description and they returned my money, telling me to go ahead and throw away the item. Thanks, Amazon!

I love Walker's Shortbread. Consistently great ingredients and taste. I also love mincemeat pie so much I'll make it before apple or any other kind, any day. So, how could I not love these tasty looking little mincemeat "pies" made with shortbread for crust!

They were shipped well without any crumbling and arrived on time. These sit within tiny aluminum type pie pans. Some noted mold on the little pans underneath the filling so I checked that first. No mold; they were clean and unblemished. Reviewers recommended microwaving them a few seconds to warm them up. But I couldn't get them out of the little pie pans without breaking the "pie" in half or knocking off all the top crust. I looked inside to find the mincemeat all dried up and stuck to the bottom. It was so dry, it was actually hard. I tried a bite anyway and it had a pronounced metallic taste. Obviously the little pie pans had leached into the mincemeat. I couldn't find a "Best By" date on the box so I don't know if this is a time problem for Walkers or a weather problem.

Suffice it to say, though these had great potential, they were totally inedible. I threw them all away. Such a waste of money and resources.

Like another reviewer, we only have home-made bread in our house and have not bought a loaf of bread in 30 years. So, I am an experienced bread maker.
My first loaf of bread, made with a favorite recipe failed. While it did rise, the texture was similar to a "quick" bread made with baking powder. (I use my KitchenAid to kneed for about 8 minutes, then do a final 5 or 6 minute hand kneed to check for "feel" of the dough.) We made two sandwiches from it, then fed the rest to the goats.
I went to the Great River Organic Milling web-site to look at their recipes and made one using my KitchenAid rather than a bread machine. Once again, the texture was unacceptable. Finally, I made a honey/butter french bread from a recipe we have been using for years. While the dough rose during the pre-shaping rise, after shaping it went to sleep. When it was finally double in bulk I baked it -- and once again -- good taste, but quick bread texture.
An other reviewer has had similar problems.
So, what to do with the 20 pound of flour you have left? I have found that the flour makes great crackers --olive oil, flour water and what ever seasonings and flavors you want. (My recipe comes from Fine Cooking, but there are many on the web.) The Great River Bread flour can also be used in several of the recipes in "Simply Great Breads[[ASIN:1600852971 Simply Great Breads: Sweet and Savory Yeasted Treats from America's Premier Artisan Baker]]It works in the crescent rolls (pg 58) and in the flatbreads beginning on page 75.
I hope this comment helps other like me that have a great deal of bread flour that they do not wish to use in "regular" bread. I'm down to 15 pounds left to go!

I was excited to come across this but then started to see red flags as soon as I got it.

First, the website on the front of the box goes nowhere, and a Google search only revealed a few nutrition websites referencing this product. I couldn't find any direct link to the brand.

Second, they have recipes inside of the box with incorrect net carb counts. I track net carbs pretty closely using an app and, even when using the lowest carb version of each ingredient on the market, found that the calculations are just flat out wrong.

Third, eating Carbquik threw me right out of ketosis, even though I followed all the low-carb rules. I've been strictly adhering to 20 grams of net carbs daily and I've been measuring my ketones regularly. Carbquik is the only thing that changed.

I definitely understand the struggle to find good low-carb food (I've been low-carbing for years, having once lost 80 pounds). I'd stay away from this one though if you want to keep your diet on track.

Unrelated tip: Try getting the CarbManager app. They have TONS of low-carb recipes that are fantastic AND accurate.

At first glance you'll notice pods are packaged in an airtight container to help preserve freshness. Using the espresso setting, you'll receive a weak shot of espresso, even with the more intense roasts. The lungo setting makes a decent cup of instant coffee, comparable to using a Keurig pod machine. It does not have the depth of the original nespresso pods.

I descale the Pixie every 3 months. Upon moving the machine I realized the machine has been leaking. I did not have this issue with the Nespresso pods. The Pixie is one of the lower end models, so I would assume using third party pods can cause issues with the pressure. The machine was on a wood countertop, small island cart from Target, and has been absorbing the leaking water for the past month. I've ordered more Nespresso pods direct from Nespresso and will update the post if leaking continues. Trying to save a few pennies per shot can cause more damage than it's worth. Buyer beware.

This is a wonderful product. I voted one star in hopes people will read this. The "lumps" in the mix are Belgian sugar crystals. They are supposed to be there. If you cook it properly they will melt and coat the waffle is a delicious brown caramelized coating. It does take some effort to get off of your waffle iron but it come clean by merely soaking in warm water. The mix does not pour like US waffle mix, it is the consistency of soft cookie dough and there things are heaven.

Be careful. Item pictured shows the label: "Contains no MSG."

The actual product received says, "No MSG added."

There is a difference. When it's stated that it's not "added" it CAN mean that it's in there by way of some of the other ingredients it contains.

The "contains no MSG" was a clear indication that the product was entirely free of MSG.

For those with allergies to MSG, this is an important distinction.

Q: What did I like about the product?
A: It was shipped quickly. The Amazon box was undamaged. A refund was promptly issued.
Q: What did I dislike about the product?
A: Both bags were "inflated", just like a bag of potato chips you may have experienced on a commercial flight. This is evidence that the vacuum seals are NOT intact. When I gently squeezed the unopened bags, I could hear the gas escaping from the unopened bags. (Additionaly, the Gran Espresso bag did have a competent valve, but nevertheless, a leak somewhere else on the bag.)
Q: How fresh was the product?
A: As indicated by the date on the bag, they were well over a year old upon receipt. (Sorry, I threw the bag out without photographing the dates.)
Q: How did the beans taste?
A: Before tossing them into the trash can, I drew a few shots through our machine. I was simply curious regarding the taste and crema. The taste was of old, improperly stored, clearly NOT fresh beans.
Q: How was the crema?
A: The crema was very weakly present, barely evident, and consistent with a drawl from old & stale beans.
Q: How do I know what fresh beans taste like?
A: We've been making espresso at home for 17 years. In fact & quite importantly, we intermittently roast our own beans at home. Because we've roasted our own beans, I've seen multiple times, & through this experience understand, how the crema develops with freshly roasted beans. (Try roasting your own beans, & the insightful understanding gained will be an epiphany.)
Synopsis:
We are experienced espresso comsumers. We are not snobs, though we are educated and proficient. We are NOT fools. **We recieved two bags, (four kilos of roasted beans). Both bags had incompetent seals. Both had stale beans.

With each additional bite, the texture and flavore became worse and worse. I cooked it al dente because I knew it was going to be in my steaming sauce so it might continue to soften. With each fork full, the pasta started to crumble and that, along with the flavor began to resemble something like that of wet all purpose flour with a little bit of bite. The pasta crumbled in my mouth into something paste-like. And I'm not referring to how when foods are chewed, it gets mulched down with your saliva to ease the passage down your esophagus. It literally felt like the product was losing every last bit of moisture the more you chewed it. That was a rough serving of spaghetti to put down.

I didn't want to be wasteful though so I gave it another chance after it sat drained for about a couple hours. When I put the sauce in it this time the same thing happened. It seemed to have pulled out whatever water was in the pasta and made my sauce very watery. The pasta was even more brittle and crumbled apart even faster. I could not stomach that serving and threw it away. I felt sad that I wasted my tasty sauce.

If I could give a negative rating, I absolutely would.  I love beef jerky and beef sticks and decided to give the original flavor a whirl...oh how I wish I would have kept my hard earned $20. I took one from the box and opened it up and went to take a bite, but before I even got it to my mouth to try it, I got a whiff of it and it honestly made my stomach clench. I have it a go anyway since there are many foods that don’t smell all that great but taste wonderful (big mistake man, big, big BIG mistake. I should have spit it out IMMEDIATELY but I am obviously a glutton for punishment.  That beef stick was just plain foul. I can’t even fully come to terms with what happened to my poor taste buds. It’s like the layer of grease permeated the taste buds with mini Velcro because just from that one awful bite I could not get rid of that horrid taste. I was honestly nauseous for well over an hour. I rank that thing right up there with peas. Green beans, canned spinach, sauerkraut, pickled beets and my moms sugar browned potatoes.....alll nasty and inedible. I split the rest up between my dogs and tossed the wrapper in my recycling bag.  Today I am cleaning up my kitchen and I keep smelling something really icky, I looked everywhere and could not find the source. I took the garbage out, that wasn’t it. Checked the litter box, nope. Looked around for “surprise gifts” left by my dogs, not that either. I figured maybe something spoiled in the pantry, the smell was much stronger over here.  I just emptied, purged and rearranged my pantry a few days ago so I find that very hard to believe. As I shut the doors I got a huge whiff of the bad smell. The recycling bag hangs from the handle of the pantry...I stuck my head in the bag (why oh why did I have to do this to myself for goodness sake) and sniffed....and gagged. I couldn’t figure out what I put in there that smelled so awful, until I pulled out that dang meat stick wrapper.  I had to put the wrapper into a baggie just so I wouldn’t smell it anymore.  Suffice it to say that if this is what “healthy” food tastes and smells like, I will loose so much weight because I won’t be able to stomach it. I will take my full fat, full flavor tastes and smells so dang good and gladly knock 10 years off of my life, rather than trying to stomach that nastiness

The ad states a "Set of 4" and a "Pack of 4" which, to them, means the same thing.  However, the word "set" implies TWO OR MORE matched units sold together whereas a "pack" would mean individual units grouped together.  So, by this logic, a "Pack of 4" should be FOUR units and a "Set of 4" should be EIGHT or more units.  The other issue is that a "Set of 4" is more expensive than the "Pack of 4" which would indicate that you would be receiving more of the product.  However, that is false.  Whether you order a "Set of 4" or a "Pack of 4" you get the same amount.  That is misleading and deceptive advertising.

Working from home has provided me a glimpse into the day of a young girl and her after school snack.

My young daughter loves Flaming Hot Cheetos so asked if I would get a box of mac and cheese with the same flavor. She was so excited to try this amazing ingenuity of man kind. She asked if she could make it right after school for a "snack". "Sure", and I didn't give it a second thought. While making it I could hear her making dry heave sounds coming from the kitchen. I hollered "are you ok in there?" In an attempt to catch her breath I hear "yeah, it just smells pretty bad" as she gasps of air.

A few minutes later I heard a sound that can only be described as an old man throwing up, mixed with a screeching cat! That was enough to get me up from working and walk toward the kitchen. I was met as she was running out of the kitchen. With watery eyes , her tongue attempting to climb out of her mouth to freedom and a plea from her face to be rescued from the dumpster of rotten school milk that now was the smell of our kitchen. I had to laugh.

She continued to give me the detailed experience that lead to this horrific end. She said as she mixed the mac and cheese, it smelled pretty bad, "you know how some things don't look good or smell the best but still taste ok?" was her first statement. I nodded my head. Then she blurted out, "it stunk so bad I could taste the smell.... in my mouth!"

Needless to say this did not get the stamp of approval and now is officially banned by my young daughter to every come back into the house again!

He always checks labels and ingredients for anything I eat. We were very surprised to see that semolina wheat flour is one of the first ingredients. Mystery solved and to all celiacs out there, please be aware. I was concerned about my husband’s pending surgery and in a hurry and wasn’t as diligent as I usually am when ordering. I have and continue to pay the price for my mistake. To Amazon, please correct the advertising for this item and ensure that your vendors have vetted product descriptions for accuracy. Fortunately, celiac disease does not lead to anaphylaxis when you are poisoned with gluten. It does however lead to stomach cancer and causes intense pain for months after consumption. I have the test vial with sample and the reading on my Nima tester and could seek legal advice but as long as the description is corrected, I have no intention of doing so. I should have been more careful with my health and know better since this isn’t the first time incorrect ingredient lists and/or advertising has lead me to consume gluten. I will not be purchasing this brand again.

At first, I had great hesitation on using this product because I was afraid that it would be like other "pre-cooked" food where the flavor really suffers and doesn't taste as good as what it would if you made it yourself. I am pleased to say, however, that I was pleasantly surprised by just how good this was as well as how well it was made and how long it has lasted (when frozen). it is literally many layers of bacon (forgot how many but like 6+) seperated by a white sheet of... wax paper-ish material?

Each layer had a full row of bacon (at least a dozen slices), is super easy and simple. Can grab one or two slices out of the freeze and throw into the microwave for roughly 10 seconds (on high) then straight onto the top of a burger (or take a few more slices and make a BLT, or use them to wrap your chicken in before baking, or anything else you might think of) with complete ease without the mess or time it would take to make it otherwise. It lasts a really really long time when frozen as well. The last thing I have to say is that the bacon actually has a rather good amount of actual bacon and not a lot of fat on the strips which is another huge plus.

Solid quality product in my personal opnion and would (easily) buy again in the future when I run out. This is not to say this is better than any bacon you could personally cook as you might be a good cook, but if you're looking for a quality substitute due to time limits or just want to simplify things for yourself, I would recommend this product.

I am 100% sold on the Chebe brand. For most of the products, it may seem like an acquired taste (getting used to the tapioca flour and the way it cooks). This product, Chebe Bread Focaccia Flat Bread, seemed like a perfect idea for pizza and sandwiches or wraps. We own a Presto Pizza Pizzaz and it worked perfectly. I recommend putting a sheet of foil on the pizzaz plate/or pizza pan if cooking in the oven. I mixed the Chebe in a Kitchen Aid and then rolled it out into a thin circle (we like thinner crusts). Unlike most Gluten Free pizza crust mixes, Chebe's actually stays thin. It doesn't bake up like a cake, like the Gluten Free Pantry brand does. We use WalMart brand pizza sauce (GF) and cheese, and put on the toppings of our choice. It cooks perfectly and tastes great. There are italian spices already in the mix that taste delicious, you just add egg, oil, and parmesan cheese. It's quick and simple!

Pros:
- Cooks flat as a pizza crust should
- Mix tastes great with spices infused
- Works best for pizza, sandwiches, and wraps
- Makes two 12-14", thin crust pizzas (we usually eat one and put the 2nd crust in a baggie in the fridge to make a few days later)

Cons:
- Chebe used to hide their ingredients lists in the recipe, but this new packaging actually lists it at the top, which is helpful!
- Can't think of anything else...it's that good.

Let me start by saying that Ive been vegan for over 2 decades now (I'm 33BTW), and first tried Nooch (that's nutritional yeast) about 8 years ago, and didn't really dig it,may have been using incorrectly or just my taste buds being different. However since then I have tried a few different kinds ( think the big names, but I'm not going to say which ones here). This brand by far is the best tasting. It is smaller flakes, more ground up to a flour almost, then what I'm use to....that's okay tho, because Nooch is going to "melt/blend" into whatever you put it on or in. AND it keeps it's taste once blended in, where some brands I've had lose a lot of flavor once mixed, or need a high quantity of Noosh to be able to taste it. I used it the first day I got it in a huge salad and then on my vegan chilli. I'd start an Instagram page just to  show case this product, if the company sponsered it 🤗 it's that good. I could eat it out of the bag. I do catering part time, and all my food is vegan, this is going to open the door for so many new dishes. For those who had a bad experience, I would say give it any other try. If you are looking for cheese flavor and have had dairy recently, it's not going to taste like "cheese", which for most people involve the texture aspect too.

I loved these fennel seeds. They were big, fresh, lively, beautiful, sweetly aromatic--just so nice (nothing like the store-bought varieties, which are so dried up and small, with only a faint lingering smell of fennel). Seeing a big 1 lb bag of beautiful, fresh fennel seeds sitting in my pantry, I remembered to use them for their medicinal benefits too, and, after a meal with a particular potential for upset, opened the bag and scooped a heaping spoonful of fennel seeds into a mug and poured some hot water over them, then let them sit, covered, for a few minutes. The tea worked like a charm, and I bypassed the usual bloatiness and etc that went with that particular meal (those old, dried up seeds I'd been using all along barely comforted my stomach at all, and I always just assumed it could've been much worse if I hadn't bothered to make the tea at all--these actually WORKED). The tea was incredibly tasty too, and breathing in the vapors was so pleasant and relaxing. I plan on trying them out in dukkah, a very nice Egyptian spice mix a good friend got me hooked on (and this particular brand's fennel seeds come all the way from Egypt, which will make it all the more authentic and special). My one tiny peeve was the bag these came in, as the plastic zip completely detached from the bag even while it was being very carefully opened (it's now folded down with a tiny binder clip on the end). Thankfully, the thoughtful folks at Starwest Botanicals slipped the spice bag into a larger, heftier zip lock bag with a better zip, so I wouldn't have any problem with the seeds spilling out anyway. When these are all gone, I'll be ordering another bagful from Starwest via Amazon, as these are not only the freshest and best quality, but also incredibly economical and much more eco-friendly, considering the cost and waste of those tiny little store-bought  glass bottles with the plastic caps that I'll never have to buy again. Save your container of store-bought fennel when you're done with it, then use this product as a refill. You'll be so happy you did. We don’t use much salt in our cooking, mainly because we typically load our ethnic dishes with so many exotic spices that adding salt would be overkill. But we always have a few types of salt on hand—French Kosher sea salt, Hawaiian black salt and Himalayan pink salt at the moment, for example—for those times when it’s absolutely necessary. This Purelife Cappadocian Spring Kosher Salt is a great addition to our culinary ingredient repertoire.

It’s definitely different than all the other salts that I’ve ever used. I can’t describe its unique taste in detail, but its in-your-face saltiness belies assertive, distinctive flavor complexities that elevate it far above the level of a mere commodity.

It comes in a nice ceramic-grinder-top plastic jar that very efficiently deposits just as much finely ground salt exactly where you want it. The grinding coarseness doesn’t appear to be adjustable—at least, I haven’t found a way to change it—but the setting is just right for most uses, neither too coarse nor too fine.

It doesn’t affect my rating, but I love all things Turkish, having taken one of the most enjoyable, memorable hiking trips in my life there years ago—including in Anatolia, where this salt comes from—and we sometimes prepare authentic Turkish dishes, so it’s neat beyond words to be able to use genuine Turkish salt on those occasions.

For its unique flavor characteristics and well-designed, functional packaging, I enthusiastically give this salt a well-deserved five-star rating.

In England Chinese food is Hong Kong style which is more of an hybrid of British and Chinese Food, there’s no better demonstration of this than curry sauce and chips. There’s a Chinese takeaway near my parents house in England that has the best curry sauce and chips I’ve ever had, admittedly there’s a lot of other takeaways that has great curry sauce and there’s plenty that have great chips but getting them both right is an art in itself. This sauce of course in no way compares, but for some reason I’ve always been a fan, mainly because I don’t take it too seriously. If You want something closer to an authentic taste the best available is the Mayflower Chinese sauce mix. McConnells is good, but it’s closer to Indian curry than Chinese which is what this sauce mix attempts to recreate. I’m not much of a curry snob and tend to cycle through them all, including the house brand. These sauces are what they are, nothing recreates the experience of walking out of the takeaway with a warm parcel of Chinese curry sauce and chips on a cold night watching coronation street.

I frequently add this bone broth powder to smoothies and soup‘s in particular. It’s a low-cost for 20 g of grass fed beef bone broth protein powder and no soy. With various allergies and taste preferences I do not want chocolate or vanilla or other artificial flavors added to the protein. I prefer to just add a scoop directly to food I’m already cooking or blending making this perfect for me.
The directions indicate that you need to blend it in such as with the whisk to the soup because it will just clump initially in hot liquids. It’s really not that hard to use a whisk in the soup pan or deep bowl and it just sort of dissolves with no sting flavor.
A favorite place to add it for me is to smoothies to give protein with hardly any calories too what are usually my almond milk and fruit blends. When you make smoothies I highly recommend you make the entire thing and then add the scoop at the very end and just pulse it in or low level start like beginning of my ice cream setting for only a few seconds. Adding it earlier in the cycle of smoothies tends to make it very foamy. I know some suggestions are to added to coffee but I feel like I would have to put my coffee in the blender and then blend before my cup. I imagine if you had one of those handheld ones you could mix it that way. I just have not put it with coffee. It has very little flavor but I’m not sure how it would taste in the coffee.

Often, I have found that healthier snack options are not really a good replacement for the unhealthy alternative (in this case, tortilla chips. But these chips have a good crunch to them, they do taste like corn (stone-ground corn is the first ingredient), and there is an equivalent amount of salt to the amount of salt on a tortilla chip. Sweet potato is third on the list and provide a nice color and flavor and sweetness (if you like sweet potato chips). The sprouted grains give them a nice grainy crunch and the grains are large and flavorful, more than an afterthought ingredient. The ingredients are so wholesome that I can give these to my young child for a snack. And I can feel good about having them myself, especially as the portion sizes are very reasonable for a small snack or lunch accompaniment. Each small bag is 1.25 ounces, about what you might expect to find in a vending machine, and 170 calories with 9 g fat, 3 g fiber, 0 g sugar, and these percent daily values: 3% vit. a, 5% calcium, 5% iron. Overall a healthy choice and a great replacement for other chips.

Definitely, this coffee is a keeper!

This can be eaten as a pudding, or you can drink it, depending on whether you make it thick or thin. I have also make pumpkin chia pudding, which was good as well, and very filling. All in all, I think this is a good brand of chia seed for including a highly nutritious superfood into your diet. Great for Diabetics & Keto Carb Counters by Using the DASH Mini Waffle maker with Keto Waffle Mix by Birch Benders. I modified this down to single person to make three blueberry waffles. Weight 37g of the mix, put in small bowl, add 1 egg, 1 table spoon Oil (avocado, melted coconut), 1 tablespoon thick Heavy Whipping Cream, splash of water if too thick. 1/4 to 1/3 cup fresh blueberries. Add all ingredients except the blueberries and whisk well. Add blueberries and fold into batter. Batter should NOT be runny but thick and flows like cake batter. Spoon into greased hot dash waffle maker (light turns off it is ready). Do not over fill, leave edges clean of batter, when you close it, it'll fill in the waffle open spaces. Cook until it stops steaming and batter is done.  Remove waffle. Grease top and bottom (i use bacon grease, using a silicon baster). Top waffles on plate with butter (kelly gold) and finish off with sugar free maple syrup. Enjoy! 11 grams net carbs total. Not for strict Keto 20 gram/day dieters. I prefer the Breakfast/Snack 10/5g Carbs; Lunch/Snack 10/5g Carbs; Dinner/Snack 10/5g Carbs approach for Diabetics doing Beginners Keto 40-50g Carb approach. What ever works for you on your Keto/Diabetic Journey ... this is mine.

I had been curious about this sauce and TorchBearer's 'Zombie Apocalypse' for some time, but had been hesitant to try a bottle of either for a few reasons... I had had one of their other hot sauces, and was quite let down by its fruitiness/sweetness; and I was (deservedly, I would say) a bit concerned about the heat. These things combined with the price made for a tricky sell. But, I love their mustard sauces and I try to buy local as much as possible, so I was thrilled when I got to sample both of these sauces at a local event.

Long story short, I went home with two bottles of the 'Rapture.' I also enjoyed the 'Zombie Apocalypse,' but can source that easily. I don't use hot sauce too terribly much, mainly just on eggs on the weekends. I don't go too heavy on the 'Rapture,' because it is really freakin' hot. But it's manageable, my fears of it being unbearably hot were unfounded - just take it real easy until you get a sense of what you're dealing with. It's a heat that builds up, and seemingly hits different parts of the mouth and throat differently... it's very interesting, and for whatever reason, I feel like it has almost a 'balance' to it where you know it's incredibly hot, but it doesn't all hit you at the same place or the same time, making it a bit easier to deal with.

Now, I like heat, but that's not really my endgame... heat needs to complement flavor. This was where the TorchBearer hot sauce I had previously tried went wrong - as I mentioned, it was very fruity and sweet, which... I can see working in certain applications, but not on eggs! 'Rapture' has a very dry, clean taste. What I want out of a hot sauce is the flavor of peppers, and that is what I get with 'Rapture.'

In short, this stuff is very, very good. If you're interested in a ridiculously hot sauce that's also loaded with flavor, I would definitely recommend it.

My grocery store stopped selling  this product.  I tried other brands and they are not as good.  I was so happy to find this item at Amazon.com and ordered the last 3 they had in stock.  It arrived on time and in good condition.  Lipton vegetable soup mix is not just for making soups and dips.  Last year I experimented with it and used it in my slow cooker with turkey.  I will take a turkey wing and thigh, place it on a couple of yams and cut up carrots.  I then pour a package of Lipton vegetable soup mix over it and let it cook for a few hours.  The turkey is so tender and has a great flavor along with the vegetables.  Do not even have to add water as the liquid from the turkey and vegetables makes a gravy which you can later add some flour and chicken broth to make a better gravy.  I have even tried adding fresh green beans while cooking, which is good. Add the green beans on top of the turkey and then pour the soup mix.  The green beans tend to fall apart if they are on the bottom.  I also tried mixing the soup mix with a can of cream of celery soup and pouring it over the turkey and vegetables.  Sometimes I'll make a green bean casserole. Depending on the size of your slow cooker, you can use whatever turkey parts you want. You can use whatever kind of fresh vegetable you want.  I am thinking of trying acorn squash or butternut squash.  I make this a couple of times a month. I have even put this on to cook with the turkey frozen when I decided last minute to make this. I hope this seller continues to carry this item as I will purchase again.

I have found many different uses for these delicious, hulled sesame seeds. They are an excellent topping for salads and casseroles, terrific for making sesame-seed crackers, and a tasty addition to veggie burgers. I have also ground them up and used them in homemade tahini.

For anyone who might be interested, I have included below my recipe for veggie burgers using these sesame seeds.

Veggie Burgers

Yield: 20 patties of 1/2 cup each
Calories: 227 per pattie

Ingredients

2 15-ounce cans pinto beans OR 3-1/2 cups cooked pinto beans
1/2 cup (96 grams) ground chia seeds
1/4 cup purified water
2 tablespoons apple cider vinegar (I use Bragg’s)
10 cloves garlic OR 1 teaspoon garlic powder
2 cups chopped, raw, green onion
1-inch piece (1 tablespoon chopped) fresh ginger OR 1/4 teaspoon ginger powder
1 cup rolled oats
1 cup (127 grams) walnuts
1 cup (133 grams) sunflower seeds
1/2 cup (72 grams) hulled sesame seeds
1-1/8 cup cooked quinoa
1 tablespoon tomato powder OR 1 tablespoon ketchup
1/4 cup nutritional yeast
1/4 teaspoon stevia OR 1 teaspoon sugar OR 1 teaspoon honey
1 teaspoon smoked paprika
1 tablespoon cumin
1 teaspoon Mrs Dash SW Chipotle
1/2 teaspoon salt
1/2 teaspoon pepper

Instructions

•Add the ground chia seeds to the water and vinegar, stir well, and set aside. The chia will rapidly begin to gel. This thickener is the magic ingredient that helps the burger patties to stick together and hold their shape.
•Drain the beans, rinse them thoroughly, place them in a bowl, and mash them into a chunky pulp.
•Pulse in a food processor (or blender) until coarsely ground: garlic cloves, fresh ginger, green onion, oats, walnuts, sunflower seeds, sesame seeds and quinoa.
•Combine all the ingredients together, mixing well to create a dense, chunky mixture.
•Grease trays on which to form burger patties. (I use stainless steel toaster oven trays.) Use a 1/2-cup measuring cup or, ideally, a jumbo, triggered, cookie-dough dipper. Scrape the top of the measuring cup or dipper with a knife or spatula for a consistent measurement. Form each patty into a round, flat, burger shape, about 1/2-inch thick.
•Place the of patties in the freezer to harden for at least 20-30 minutes.
•Toaster oven 400 degrees: Bake the patties on greased toaster-oven trays while they are still partially frozen for 10 minutes per side, until they are browned and firm.
•Air fryer 400-degree, air-fry setting: Remove the wire-mesh trays and use only the bottom tray. Though it has a non-stick coating, grease it anyway to insure the burgers will not stick. Cook the patties while they are still partially frozen, 10 minutes per side, for a total of 20 minutes, until they are browned and firm. Use a metal spatula to carefully insert the patties into the air fryer, to turn them, and to remove them when done. Use a silicone spatula to re-grease the bottom tray for each successive batch of patties. Reduce cooking time by 1-2 minutes for each consecutive batch to achieve the same results.
•Leftover patties can be frozen and quickly thawed and heated up for subsequent meals.

I am a big tea drinker, and coffee, too. I have possibly 10-15 different coffee and tea in the cabinet at any given time. So when I saw this, and that it was from Taiwan, where it is known for good tea, I thought to give it a try.
It arrived well packaged, and the actual package looks very presentable. If you were choosing this as a gift, it would be perfect. Sadly, my wife had the first drink while I was at work, but she did tell me it was pretty good, so I gotta try.
There are two different types of tea, rolled or just plain roasted. This happens to be plain roasted (not rolled) so I tend to put a little bit more. Now, people would argue the best way to have tea, for me, I use a French press. I don't drink coffee with it, but tea and tea only. It allows the tea leaves to have a chance to fully relax, and unwind, thus, give you the full favor, or the lack of.
This tea smells somewhat sweet, just a tad. But when you drink it, it has a very full-bodied taste, and not too sweet. I prefer to have my tea "as-is" meaning no sugar no milk (though, my wife like to add milk, and I tired it, it was good), just plain tea.
Overall, I think this tea is really good, well worth the price and also the taste. It is good for your own taste as well as gifting, since the season is upon us.
Oh, and if you like, I suggest to do a second round, but cool it to make iced black tea, it is of course lighter, but gives a totally different yet somewhat familiar feeling to the tea.

I feel guilty whenever I don't brew it gongfu cha style, which easily produces 6-8 steepings.
Make sure you don't use water that is too hot, 185 should be ideal, and don't steep for too log - I recommend about 1.5 for the first steeping, and 15-20 for each one after that, steeping longer once the tea gets weaker. If you have friends who are connoisseurs of oolong, invite them for a treat!

Let's face it... YES & absolutely: Fiji water is on the expensive side.  But there's just nothing else like it.  I used to call my partner (husband) and our friends "Water Snobs" because whenever we went out to eat, they would always request either Fiji or Voss.  So, one evening I decided to administer a taste-test to prove to them (OK, really prove to myself) that they couldn't tell the difference between various waters.  Fiji, Voss, Deer Park, Tap & GE Monogram purified water from our refrigerator were all left out to be room temp for about 1/2 hour.  To my absolute surprise & disbelief, they were able to distinguish which water was what each time with the exception of Tap vs. Refrigerator water.  I was just certain that I could curtail the expense of ordering blinged-out H2O when we dined out -- -- but, how in the world could they tell the difference??  So, a personal taste-test was obviously in order.  Sure enough, I too, was able to clearly distinguish between the waters [again] with the exception of Tap vs. Refrigerator water, which makes since.  I mean, how much purification really happens from your fridge, right?  Fiji is truly the smoothest, most velvety-textured water I've ever had.  I used to be not much of a water drinker.  I know, "Hydrate or Die".  But, ever since being properly introduced to the finer side of water...I too, must divulge, have in-fact: become a water-snob.  Pity...I really shouldn't have ever questioned.  Now I'm stuck with Subscribe & Save monthly Fiji water deliveries for the rest of my life.  ;-)

I got my water kefir grains about 4 months ago. About 1/4 cup. They arrived quickly, and packaged well. I immediately followed the directions on the poseymom website. I have been making fizzy water kefir using frozen mango cubes and sliced peaches, and I add a squirt of lemon after fermenation is done, right before I put it in the fridge. I got some good sealing bottles to put the drink in so it stays fizzy.

I find I can't drink it fast enough, and the water kefir grains just keep growing and growing. I even didn't make any for a month, and had to travel with them when I moved across the country and live in a hotel with no fridge for 3 weeks and I just had them in sugar water in a jar with a paper towel and rubber band to seal the top, put it in a cooler with ice. They stayed alive that whole time.

I make water kefir drink for a week or two, then put the grains in the fridge to rest while I finish drinking what's in all my bottles.

I've been putting grains in my morning smoothie lately. I now decided I'm going to just eat the grains for probiotics for awhile, because I struggle with some sort of fungal growth inside my body, maybe Candida albicans, maybe a few different ones, but I'm not sure about the yeast in the drink, and it seems the jury is 50/50 on the subject of whether that's OK. I know the yeast is different in the water kefir than the yeast parasite that's in my body, but just to be sure, I'm gonna not make the water kefir drink for about a month or two, and just eat the grains, see how that goes.

I'm going to just keep making the sugar water for the grains so they keep multiplying so I have enough to eat. Most of the time I use raw turbinado sugar to feed them. Sometimes brown sugar. I also sometimes add a pinch of baking soda, or a pinch of salt.

After about 4 months, I currently have more than 6 times the amount I received from poseymom, and that's after eating at least a half a cup since receiving them! I really have no idea how much I've consumed. I don't currently have anyone to give them to, so I'm fine with just eating them in smoothies, and it's a good way to sneak more probiotics into my husband!

If I find I'm getting too many grains in the jar, I can just let them rest in the fridge. I can still spoon some out with my wooden spoon while they're resting in the fridge because they're still alive, just not multiplying so much!

Thanks poseymom for an easy and inexpensive way for me to get more probiotics!

I absolutely love avocado oil, and have had nothing but good experiences with La Tourangelle over the past 5 or 6 years. One of the biggest challenges when buying exotic oils, is figuring out what to use it for without feeling like you're wasting it. As a general rule, I use avocado oil and a great quality extra virgin olive oil interchangeably.The color is a beautiful shade of green, the taste has the distinctive creamy and slightly grassy/slightly sweet taste of avocados. It's great on salads, to dip bread into, or drizzled on soups or stews. I've also cooked with it when the flavor of avocado will pair nicely. I tend to use it in Latin American dishes, because I follow the rule of "if it grows together it goes together." One thing that is different about avocado oil vs olive oil, is La Tourangelle recommends it is kept refrigerated after opening. The first time I purchased, I kept it in the cupboard with other oils and didn't notice a significant different in flavors, nor did it appear to go rancid any faster than when I kept it in the fridge, but I may use it more than a typical home cook. Since it's kept in the fridge, it will solidify making it impractical to just grab and add to what it is you're cooking. So I usually take a 4 cup measuring cup and fill it 1/3 with warm water and put the can of oil right into it for a few minutes to liquify the oil, then use as normal. I'm not an expert in food or medicine, but there's a general consensus among people far more qualified than me of health benefits associated with avocado oil. It is made up of monounsaturated fatty acids which reduce inflammation, assist in decreasing LDL, and assist in increasing HDL; it's rich in antioxidants; and it contains compounds beneficial to fighting liver damage. The bottom line is, if you like avocados and are looking for an alternative oil to add to your cooking, this is a reasonable size container of avocado oil at a reasonable price.

Mega Death is that next gradation of heat, spice, and taste. Really tasty, the single-most important criterion when picking a sauce. It adds distinct flavor and, when properly used, gives you the blend of heat and spice that turns you into an addict. You could literally overindulge with a good sauce, so be careful.

I have to revert to my one- or three-drop amounts, and that's not only economical but good sense when dealing with Blair's sauces. If not graduallly tested, you could end up eating grass instead of salsa, and that's not a good way to get fiber.

I've tried San Francisco Bay's Breakfast Blend, Rainforest, Donut Shop and Fog Chaser. This French Roast is closest to the Fog Chaser, but a little bit smoother. Of course, coffee tastes are somewhat subjective, but I've enjoyed each SFB cup I've tried. And I'm baffled by those who declare this the world's worst coffee and say it's absolutely undrinkable. They might have more refined coffee palates than I do.

There are some objective aspects of the SFB coffee experience that can be addressed--especially in light of some of the other reviews on here. First, I've been brewing SFB kcups in my Keurig every day (sometimes twice a day) for almost a full year and I've NEVER had one of the cups leak, back flow or otherwise not work. Nor have I experienced any inconsistency in the taste of the cups. I'm sure this does happen occasionally (as it probably does with all brands), but I've probably brewered close to 400 cups of SFB coffee without a single problem.
Second, it should be pretty clear from the image provided by amazon that these are not the typical k-cups. In fact, SFB prides itself on being somewhat environmentally friendly--hence the lack of a plastic bottom to their "one cups." The design requires that you store the coffee in a cool, dry environment and preferably in an airtight container (no different from the requirements of storing loose grounds). Fortunately, when you buy the box of 80 (and get the very good per pod price), they come wrapeed in airtight, light-blocking bags of 8. Open one bag, put the 8 pods in an airtight container and throw it in the fridge. Simple...and stays fresh.

Take a shot on these--I don't think you'll be disappointed. If you like a lighter roast, I recommend the Breakfast Blend (over the Donut Shop). If you like darker, try Fog Chaser or the French Roast (or maybe the Espresso....but I haven't tried that one yet).

I was fortunate enough to encounter one of the members from the Perfect Foods Bar family at my local market, giving samples of four different bars. But I didn't like them just for the protein, I like the idea that I'm getting a lot of nutrients here too, with tomato, kelp, egg, kale, carrots, apple, and a lot more, none of which comes to the fore in flavor. The flavor is excellent. This is something you could cut up and give to your kids as an after school treat. They'd love it and you could feel good about it.

The price here is a bit higher than what I was paying locally, though I understand you can sometimes find these at Costco for about half what I've paid. If you consider that each bar is really a meal substitute, or several snacks worth of food, then the price doesn't really seem that outrageous.

This is my third order from Amazon for this product. When I decided to go wheat free a few months ago I knew I had to come up with an acceptable pancake mix because I LOVE pancakes. Since I'd used Bisquick for many years my first experiment was naturally to go with their gluten-free product. It was okay but nothing to brag about. I still have a partial box left over that I use sometimes as a coating for fish or chicken.

So I got to looking some more and kept coming across reviews for Pamela's Baking & Pancake Mix. There were a lot of positive reviews so I gave it a shot and have been very satisfied. Blueberry pancakes almost every morning. No kidding! I use milk instead of water (water and pancakes just don't seem right together to me) and add lots of blueberries and a couple tablespoons of chia seed. For the oil I use coconut oil. My wife made some chocolate chip cookies with it and they were pretty excellent too. Now that the weather is getting cooler, we'll be experimenting more.

I've recommended this mix to several family members and others and they are on board with it. Most of them are not on gluten-free diets but agree that it's a healthy alternative to wheat-based products. My wife and I and our two adult children are also not gluten intolerant.

The only negative I have about this product is the packaging. The three bags may be shipped in frustration-free packaging but the packages themselves are not frustration-free. I usually give up trying to pinch the seals together and just fold the top over. But still, this is five-star in my book. I did find this mix at a local grocery store but by ordering it though Amazon I saved about ten dollars for three bags.

I didn't realize that this was 'the' brand to use for making arepas, but it doesn't surprise me at all to find out. My friends and I used to use Maseca when we made arepas on the weekends, or the morning after a party at our house to fuel the clean-up effort and for whomever was still hanging around. After more than half a decade of doing this we stumbled upon PAN and realized just how much better it is at making a beautiful smooth almost creamy masa. The results are not even comparable. Luckily we can get it quite easily in any grocery store in or around DC, I'm sorry to here that you have a hard time finding it in CA-- that's surprising. So this review is really for comparison of brands. So as far as that's concerned, this is it. If you are thinking of ordering corn flour/corn meal on the internet for making tamales, arepas, tortillas, etc. this is the brand.

And since I'm writing a review anyhow, I might as well share, this is how we make arepas:

Mix PAN white corn meal with water and a bit of salt to make a masa (dough) which should be wet enough to easily form into thick smallish pancake like forms in your hands, but shouldn't come off in little globs sticking to your fingers. However you will get sticky hands eventually. Cook these on a medium heat using a cast iron skillet lightly greased with olive oil until the arepas are nicely browned on both sides, then transfer them to the oven to keep warm while you finish the rest. I like to make my arepas fairly thick, about 3/4" and 5-6" in diameter. Made that way not many people can eat more than 2, because then of course there are the fillings....

Grate some fresh mozzarella cheese, put 2-3 cans of [[ASIN:B0005YL6TA Goya Black Beans - 24 Pack]] in a pot with chopped green onion and a little salt. Simmer on a medium low heat like that until they look and taste done. They should be served hot so if they finish before everything else is ready just re-heat them before serving.

Guacamole and salsa are also a must, and you can have a little extra chopped cilantro on the table for people to add if they like.

For the salsa, chop about one small red onion very finely. If you find raw red onion too sharp a taste you can soak it, once it's chopped, briefly in a bowl with salt water to draw out some of that intensity. Finely dice 3-4 large ripe tomatoes removing most of the watery bits. Mix with the red onion, juice of half a lime, add some chopped cilantro and salt and pepper to taste. Only add the salt just before serving as it will draw out the juices in the tomatoes. Or instead add half - 1 pack of Goya Sazón [[ASIN:B000SW1GSU Goya Sazon Goya Clntro/achte, 1.41-Ounce Units (Pack of 36)]].

For the guacamole, use 5 ripe avocados chopped and then continue to mash with your hands. I usually give this job to some poor helplessly polite and obliging guest, but trust me it tastes better that way. Not when a guest does it but when it's done by hand. You still get some nice chunks because hands just can't squeeze it all out before even the most obliging guest will ask to be excused, but it's still nice and smooth. Come on, don't be so fastidious! They'll wash their hands! Season with finely chopped cilantro, fresh lime juice (the importance can not be stressed enough of only ever using freshly squeezed lime juice, whether you're making a gin and tonic or guacamole-- no exceptions. And the same goes for lemon juice.), continue seasoning with salt and cumin powder. Add to all of this some finely diced tomatoes and even more finely chopped red onion as well as some completely pulverized jalepano and you'll have a killer guac.

All of these things can be put out in bowls for guests to add to their arepas in whatever combination or ratios they prefer. But if you're taking beans and cheese I don't know why you would put them next to each other so that the warm delicious re-fried beans can slightly melt the cheese. Like I said before, you can also have a small bowl of chopped cilantro and or chopped green onion and or sour cream for people to add as well.

I've tried every bread under the sun, on various diets. For quite a while I ate gluten-free breads. Of these (not low-carb), I found Three Bakers breads and Canyon Bakehouse breads the best. But now I've gone Keto/Atkins, and this corn loaf is my favorite, I'm SO glad I found it. It is gluten-free AND low-carb, a staple of my diet. Each slice provides 39% of the MDR of B1, key to burning carbohydrates for fuel and providing usable energy, and 20% of B2, which increases oxygen availability in cells and the bloodstream. The bread comes in very convenient plastic tubs which prevent it from being squashed (especially handy for stocking up, stacking in the freezer).

The slices are small and it is slightly dry and crumbly (very similar to the texture of English Muffin bread at Food-for-Less, if you've ever tried that) but I vastly prefer it to the somewhat slimy texture of most gluten-free breads. To eat it plain, it's best if you heat it in the microwave for 5 seconds or so. It's wonderful toasted, and for grilled cheese sandwiches. But the main thing I love about it is the FLAVOR- SO good!! No weird, slightly off tang of odd grains- just a wholesome, rich taste like that of the best white bread. I just love it! For me the great taste trumps the crumbly texture. It freezes well. And with 4 net carbs per slice, I can have a slice of toast in the morning with my eggs, a grilled cheese sandwich for lunch, and bread and butter with dinner, and not exceed the limit of 20 net carbs per day that enables me to stay in ketosis and steadily lose weight, but still enjoy tasty bread, HOORAY. I HEARTILY recommend this yummy bread.

Kitchen King Whole Grain Basmati Rice is a product of India. This bulk pack of six plastic 2 pound jars came well presented with secure inner foil seals and tight lids.

Although I had tried both the Kitchen King White Basmati rice and their Brown Basmati rice and both cooked exactly as expected, I was a bit confused by the label on this golden colored Basmati rice. The cooking instructions on the label state: “For best results, soak for two hours before cooking”

Although I always thoroughly rinse my rice before cooking, I do not soak it. I use a fuzzy logic rice cooker which does have a built in soaking time. I was unsure what setting to use for this golden whole grain rice so I chose the Brown rice setting which normally takes around 80 minutes. To my surprise, the rice cooker signaled that it was done after about an hour. This rice cooked up beautifully, white and fluffy.

This is a low glycemic index whole grain rice, so it takes a bit longer to digest and leaves one feeling fuller. It is a tasty rice which turned out fluffy and flavorful. I would definitely get this variety again. The Best By date on the jars that I received is 13 months in the future.

Many people do not know much about honey except what they see in a grocery store as a thick amber colored liquid.  But I promise you that there is much more to know. What you are seeing is the crystalization of sugar coming out of the water in the honey and this is absolutely normal. ALL honey will do this!  I’ll try to explain this here and how you can easily and quickly reliquefy the sugar crystals back into the water in the honey. As you know honey is very, very sweet. It is sweeter than cane or beet sugar. That sweetness comes from an overabundance of glucose sugar molecules in the water of the honey. It is extremely concentrated sugar made that way by the bees. There is so much of an overabundance that there is an over-saturation of the water with these molecules. Honey will spontaneously on it’s own crystalize. It does this in the hive as well!  The fact is, this crystalization actually preserves the flavor and quality of the honey. I will interject here that honey is a product made by bees for THEIR survival over cold Winters… not for our survival. Remember bees get sugars in the form of nectar from the flowers that grow during Spring, Summer, and Fall, concentrate it and store it in the hive. The bees do not make their honey for mankind. In the hive the honey will be used for food to keep the bees alive. We steal part of the honey (BUT NOT ALL) for our own use but sometimes forget that it is not really being made for us humans. We are just the lucky recipients only because the beekeepers love these bees because they are so fascinating of God’s creatures. Now to change the crystals back into the water in the honey simply put the honey jar into center a saucepan. Fill the saucepan with water about half way up the uncovered glass honey jar. Do not allow any water to touch the honey! You are going to gently heat up the honey like you would heat the milk in a baby bottle. You will heat this for about 10 minutes and stir occasionally. You will note that the amber color comes back perfectly. Allow the honey to fully cool and you are done. Remember when it re-crystalizes it’s a normal thing (so don’t be surprised!)  and if you want to, you can repeat the hot water treatment again and again with no harm to the honey. Having said all this, the following is for you advanced honey students! Many people like the crystallized part of the honey because it takes much longer for it to dissolve in your mouth and allows time for the nuances of exquisite flavors to be sensed by your tongue. Something that you will not get with the liquid honey. Some advanced cooking recipes actually call for crystallized honey as an ingredient because of this. Finally, please know this. Without the bees on this earth all humans will perish. I hope that this will help someone and God Bless all including the bees!

As I write this, there are 2 unopened boxes of eco-planet hot cereal on my dining room table. In the kitchen, I have 2 more. At work, I have several packets stored in various places. Okay, I admit it, I HOARD and STASH this stuff. Why? I've been gluten free for FIFTEEN YEARS, and this is the best of the best. It is all-natural, sugar-free (I hate anything sweet for breakfast, which rules out 90% of hot cereals), high fiber, has a rich and nutty taste, and mixes instantly with hot water.

I don't just eat it for breakfast - I have it for lunch, snacks, desserts. Many criteria must be met for me to incorporate something on a daily basis, especially starches, which I hold a minor grudge against. Starches must be gluten-free, high in fiber, low in sodium, and low in sugar. Cooked starches must not leave any dishes I will have to scrub at a later time. They must not take more than 2 minutes to prepare. I wish I could find other instant cereals I love HALF this much, because eco-planet gets monotonous. I like preparing it thick (less water) with almond butter, and scooping the mixture into hollowed-out boiled egg whites. I call them "nutty caps." The cereal is also great with coconut oil and cinnamon.

For gluten-free, high-fiber instant soups, I like Taste Adventure's split pea, curry lentil, and black bean.
