Dinner tonight - stuffed Tacos!  Tried out these new Old Paso Tortilla Pockets for a change of pace from the fold-over types.  These are Flour Tortillas shaped in a Taco pocket/pouch form - each sealed all around except across the top, package of 8 .  I cooked some hamburger and chopped onions with taco seasoning, diced some fresh tomatoes, sliced some green onion, shredded some iceberg lettuce, and mixed it all up in a bowl with some sour cream, salsa, and shredded Mexican mix cheese - very simple.  Heated up 4 of the 8 Tortilla Pockets by wrapping in foil and heating for a few minutes in the oven - can also heat in microwave.  Had to let them cool for a bit before handling and stuffing.  They are thicker than regular Tortillas, but surprisingly tender. It was so easy, just spooning the mixture into the pouches.  The taste was very good, the Flour Tortilla Pockets held up pretty well, but did have a leak in one, probably caused by too much liquid from the tomatoes, or by handling it a bit too aggressive.  Going with 5 Stars, as they are unique and would work well with children - usually not as messy.

I'm completely new to kefir and the package came with really good and detailed instructions. I usually buy organic raw milk and boil it before storing in the refrigerator. So, instead of going with homogenized milk as the instructions ask for (for easy acclamation), I went straight with the organic raw milk which I normally consume. I followed the instructions in leaving it in room temperatures and refresh it every 24 hours. The first few batches didn't have the pleasant yogurt aroma. However, it didn't affect the consumption (except one time, it was bitter and I gave it to the compost).

After a few days, the kefir showed robust activity, at which time, it was hard to catch up in my consumption. And the volume of the grains grew so much that I started worry about what to do with them. I eventually put the kefir in the refrigerator as soon as the grains are mixed with fresh milk, until the day I'm ready for to "harvest" the kefir. As to the excessive grains (I see myself eventually running out of people to gift them to), I started eating them with breakfast. Sometimes, I don't even chew them and just swallow some.

It's been 3 months now and I'm really happy with the grains and they are so robust. If I have them in the refrigerator for several days without the milk (due to the pandemic), they'd go right to business as soon as milk is available. And they give me beautiful aroma that tells me that they love where they are.

I'd strongly recommend these grains.

I’ve been looking for a good “instant” coffee for camping and hiking. My main requirements were that it had to be in very light weight single serve waterproof packets and, of course, taste good. Pretty much all instant coffees can be found in single serve waterproof packets; however, the second part is questionable, especially compared to a good fresh grind pour over.

But, when on the trail, I still need a good cup of joe, even if it’s cold instant. So, I read a heap of reviews, and picked out some of the highest rated (Starbucks VIA Instant Pikes Place Medium Roast, and Mount Hagen Fairtrade Organic Instant, 25 packets for $9.95 -about 40 cents a packet), and threw in some Café Bustelo Espresso Instant Coffee someone had picked up at the local supermarket for comparison. Also bought some Starbucks VIA Instant Caffe Latte just for funzies.

- Starbucks VIA Instant Pikes Place Medium Roast, 8 packets for $5.98 or about $1.23 a packet (though you can get larger 50 count packs to get the cost down to around 80 cents a packet)
- Starbucks VIA Instant Caffe Latte, 5 packets for $5.08 - $1.02 a packet
- Mount Hagen Fairtrade Organic Instant, 25 packets for $9.95 -40 cents a packet

Over several days, my daughter and I tried the various coffees black, with half-and-half, with half-and-half and sugar, and with some Coffee Mate liquid creamer. We also compared this to some of our ground coffee. Each time, we used one packet for one cup of water.

Final verdict pretty much reflected the online reviews I had read. The Starbuck’s was the best and as good or better than a store-bought ground coffee, but still not as good as fresh ground. It was surprisingly tasty with a rich roasted slightly nutty flavor. The Mount Hagen was a close second, but had a slightly tart aftertaste like some Ethiopian Kochere coffees I’ve had -good if you like that kind of thing. We thought the Mount Hagen was just slightly weak as well, but we are partial to bolder darker roast coffees. The Mount Hagen also seemed sensitive to getting the water too hot and developing a slightly burnt taste. That’s important to me, as you can’t control the water temp too well on the trail. The Café Bustelo espresso was a weak third to the Starbucks and Mount Hagen. I know a lot of people like it, but Café Bustelo, IMHO, is somewhat of an acquired taste. If you’re cost conscious and just want a “decent” cup of coffee, I’d say go for the Mount Hagen as it’s less than half the cost of the Starbucks or Café Bustelo. If you want an instant that’s closer to a good ground drip coffee, then spend a little more and get the Starbucks.

The Starbucks Caffe Latte was not up to our expectations as far as a latte goes. It was more like a thick hot chocolate with just a hint of coffee taste. The single packets were just too much for one cup of water as it’s just too thick and almost chalky like that. I would not recommend, if you’re looking for a Caffe Latte with a good milk and coffee flavor. But mixing it with one and a half cups of water made a decent hot chocolate.

ONETANG Freeze-Dried Apple is a product of China. These single serve .35 ounce packs are a delicious and satisfying treat.

ONETANG uses lyophilization, a technique to deep freeze at very low pressure, leaving the fruit full of nutrients, vitamins and minerals. These apple pieces absolutely taste as though they have been freeze dried at the optimal time of perfect ripeness. They are naturally sweet with no added sugar.

Each 100% all apple pack contains has 35 calories, 9 grams of carbs and 85mg of potassium. This is a good low calorie treat when craving something sweet. When the bag is first opened the apple pieces are crispy. However, I got distracted and left them on a dish for a couple of hours. When I got back to them, they were soft and chewy rather than crispy but they didn’t oxidize and turn brown the way fresh apples do. They were still very tasty.

ONETANG Freeze-Dried Apple packets are a convenient way to have tasty apple pieces anywhere. The best before date on the packs that I received is 7 months in the future.

Suddenly I had no issues drinking water, because it tasted like juice!! The kicker? No sugar in these little packets. All of the deliciousness of a sugary drink without the guilt of spending precious calories.

And for this low price, you can own 44 drink packets with 4 different flavors, all of which excite the taste buds into believing you are not drinking water!! I have been drinking flavored water packets for years, and I have yet to find a better brand or a better deal than this one. This purchase is perfect for anyone who struggles with consuming their required daily amount, just wants the taste of something sweet without the harmful sugar, and makes a great gift for all those Hydroflaskers in your life.

Sadly, the one downside to this product is its bulky and wasteful packaging. The tantalizing little packets come in a large plastic container when they could easily be wrapped in something biodegradable. Regardless, the guilt of knowing you're adding waste to the Earth is easily overshadowed by the satisfaction of these low-calorie, sugarless, convenient, delicious flavor packets the second any of the flavors hit your tongue.

Review of Mazzetti Aged 3 Years Balsamic Vinegar of Modena Black Label PGI |Sweet & Thick | Perfect for Cheese & Fruit | Aged in Oak Barrels | 8.45 Ounce Bottle (Pack of 2) produced by Mazzetti and sold by World Finer Foods

I do not used balsamic vinegar very often but it is nice to have some available when the desire, need or recipe arises. Having smaller bottles is usually a waste but my usage is low enough that the smaller amounts will help reduce spoilage after opening as I will use the contents quicker.

The listed Best by date is approximately 3 years from date of receipt.

The product description includes four different varieties of Mazzetti balsamic vinegars and this is the Black Label variety.

I am not sure how they specifically prepare and process this but it appears to be a more concentrated balsamic vinegar which means that it will be thicker in consistency and perhaps have a more concentrated and intense flavor. The suggested uses are more being used to drizzle over something such as cheese. They also say drizzle over ice cream but not my preferred combination. They did not claim this but the impression is that they variety has at least started the reduction process for when a balsamic reduction is appropriate such being used as glaze.

The bottles are also very nice plus extremely dark which will help with protecting the vinegar from light although this should be stored in a cool, dry and preferably dark place.

I found the flavor to be very pleasant with a bit more wood flavor than I expected. The flavor also seemed more concentrated than the grocery store type of balsamic vinegar that I typically purchase but that is from memory, not side-by-side taste testing.

I personally choose to brew these coffee grounds in a reusable k-pod. I've found this method to be quite effective, and I've only has the tiniest bit of sediment in the bottom of my mug afterwards; Not anymore than I get with other coffee grounds. The brew I get using this method is nice and strong.

When drinking this mushroom coffee, I do get the feeling that it helps to improve mental clarity and cognition more than coffee blends I've tried that don't contain supplemental mushrooms. Caffeine on its own doesn't do too much for me, but the mushrooms seem to strengthen the effect somewhat. I'm currently in the process of fixing my sleep schedule, and this coffee is proving quite useful in keeping myself up during the day. Overall, these mushroom coffee grounds are a very tasty medium roast that serves its purpose of giving me energy, and improving focus and concentration. It produces a good strong brew when used in a single cup coffee maker, and I expect this bag of grounds to last me a while.

I use ﻿Gustus Vitae seasonings daily as the spice blends are so unique, fresh and flavorful. The blends are so good and elevate even basic veggies and other plain dishes. “Everything But the Pizza Seasoning” is an all natural blend that goes beyond the typical Italian herbal blend as it’s a mix of herbs, tomato, black pepper, red and green bell peppers, salt, sesame seeds and more (not listed in that order). It tastes great on homemade pizza as it does taste like a blend of familiar pizza seasonings but has more complexity with additions such as flavorful sesame seeds and black pepper that has an unusually spicy kick that tastes a lot like the crushed red pepper I shake on my cooked pizza. This blend adds the aroma and taste of a well seasoned pizza to veggies, pasta and so much more. Simple foods taste way more interesting.

My favorite way to use this blend beyond putting it on homemade pizza is to sprinkle it on cut up zucchini, onions, bell peppers and tomatoes sprayed with a little avocado or olive oil and then roasted in my air fryer. It makes a satisfying low cal side dish with a delicious balance of flavors and a moderately spicy kick. It also tastes yummy on avocado toast, cheese toast, omelets and more. I’m surprised the heat is only from black pepper; it seems like the most potent and fresh black pepper I’ve tasted or else my blend somehow ended up with spicy red pepper mixed in. The spices come sealed in a plastic bag to empty into a cute magnetic tin that has suggested uses on it. I keep it stuck to the side of my fridge so it’s handy. The freshness is superior to store typical bought spices, and the spices aren’t irradiated. Love it. 5 stars. Packed in California.

This is an interesting product that is made from grape must - the same base for grappa - and balsamic vinegar. It has a subdued flavor of balsamic vinegar and the added benefit of mixing well with oil.

For personal use this is wonderful as a flavor enhancer for fresh strawberries. For friends, especially those who love mixing balsamic vinegar, olive oil and spices as a bread dip, I use this instead. One reason is that it actually mixes with the olive oil, giving a more uniform dipping sauce. Of course, another reason is that it has the expected flavor that is unique to balsamic style vinegars.

I use a little of this (along with lemon juice) as a marinate before cooking the fish. This reduces the 'fishy flavor' that some of my friends dislike. However, it also enhances some types of fish, especially salmon. It's also ideal with vegetables such as zucchini, peppers, eggplant and similar to be grilled over a charcoal fire. I usually mix a little of this with some olive oil, which as I stated above, it blends with perfectly, and a little crushed garlic. Baste, grill and enjoy. Conversely, you can grill the vegetables plain and use the mixture as a dipping sauce, or just a few drops of this balsamic glaze as a condiment.

Bottom line: this has advantages over regular vinegar when you been to blend with olive oil, and it is thick and viscous, so it makes a perfect basting sauce too.

I first learned of 'sambal' while working for NATO in The Netherlands back in 1967.  The Dutch have a large population of Indonesian immigrants that took asylum in their colonial homeland after World War 2 to escape the Sukarno dictatorship.  Many had worked for the Dutch administrators, military, and businesses in the many islands comprising Indonesia that became unwelcome under their new government.  As a result, there are many Indonesian restaurants throughout The Netherlands.  Each of these serves their meals with  one to three small sauce dishes of sambal to be used with the many varieties of their food as an added spice.  Once I tried it, I was hooked.  Basically it's chopped and fried hot-to-very-hot red peppers.  I have yet to be able to handle the hottest (fried down to a black paste) but the lesser heats are not only tolerable but delicious as well.  This particular brand is excellent and very reasonably priced.  I would recommend it for anyone looking to give their Indonesian, Thai, Chinese or other Asian food a delightful zing.

Most Americans are more familiar with the [[ASIN:B000LOAN66 Huey Fong Sriracha Hot Chili Sauce (17oz)]] version of Sriracha sauce with what I jokingly called the "screaming chicken" hot sauce you see in Asian restaurants, and I've also come to like the [[ASIN:B000EISJXS Thai Sriracha Sauce - Shark Brand 7oz.]], but was stunned when I found the Shark Medium Hot Sriracha.  This is going to sound odd, but there's considerable debate over the relative merits of the Huey Fong version which is fairly thick and somewhat sweet that makes it more palatable to American tastes, and the [[ASIN:B000EISJXS Thai Sriracha Sauce - Shark Brand 7oz.]] which is is prepared in the more traditional Thai manner, meaning it is runnier and more piquant.  If you're even considering the Shark Medium Hot Sriracha then you're certainly not a novice and know what you're getting into.  You won't be put off by all the foreign language labeling and fearful of the contents.  While I like both the aforementioned Sriracha sauces and find them a great addition to Thai and Chinese dishes there are times where I really want to bring the heat.  Both of those sauces rate pretty low on the Scoville Scale of hotness, ranking in the 1,000-2,5000 range making it medium (Tabasco is the next level up).  As a self-confessed hot-head hot sauce lover I gave Shark Medium Hot Sriracha a test and have to say it is just as blendable in dishes, working in easily when cooking.  The relative hotness on the Scoville Scale is a bit tricky as it feels somewhat hotter than Tabasco yet at times about the same.  As with Tabasco a little can go a long way, but if you like it hot like me go for a splash more once the dish is finished.  I love northern Thai food and Shark Medium Hot Sriracha works well with it and with Szechwan as well.  It gives a nice pop of hot without being overpowering like the truly hot Thai chilies that rate up at 50,000-100,000 on the Scoville scale.  If something is a bit too bland for my taste usually a bit of Shark Medium Hot Sriracha gets my mouth watering. Don't let your fear of the unknown scare you off of Shark Medium Hot Sriracha as you don't know what you're missing!

FYI What dose grass fed mean?

Below is from Business Insider Mar. 25, 2016 Julia Calderone

On January 12, 2016, the Agricultural Marketing Service, a branch of the US Department of Agriculture, announced that it was dropping its official definition of "grass-fed." In a statement, the AMS claimed that it doesn't have the authority to define and determine whether specific grass-fed claims that companies make on their packaging are "truthful and not misleading."

In short, while the USDA still evaluates and approves grass-fed claims, the government no longer has an official definition of the term "grass-fed," which means the phrase is now more open to interpretation.

I LOVE CHIA SEEDS! I bought these because I was addicted to the mama chia drinks that were kind of pricey. A friend told me I could make my own by just putting chia seeds in juice and refrigerating overnight. WOW was she right, these are amazing. I also add them to my salads for a nice refreshing crunch. These can also be added to anything. I haven't tried it yet, but I really want to make chia poppy seed muffins. They sound delicious! I love that this bag brings endless possibilities!

My favorite most simple recipe:
1 cup chia seeds
3 cups orange juice
keep in fridge overnight - and you have orange flavored chia apple sauce! There's obviously no apples, but that's just what I like to call it lol.

Chia seeds are among the healthiest foods on the planet. They are loaded with nutrients that can have important benefits for your body and brain. They are tiny black seeds from the plant Salvia Hispanica, which is related to the mint. This plant grows natively in South America. Chia seeds were an important food for the Aztecs and Mayans back in the day. They prized them for their ability to provide sustainable energy… in fact, “chia” is the ancient Mayan word for “strength.” Despite their ancient history as a dietary staple, only recently did chia seeds become recognized as a modern day superfood. In the past few years, they have exploded in popularity and are now consumed by health conscious people all over the world. They are loaded with fiber, protein, Omega-3 fatty acids and various micronutrients.

Overall, I highly recommend these to anyone health conscious. Despite their tiny size, chia seeds are definitively among the most nutritious foods on the planet.
